The finding

Ask Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct to Implement a sorting algorithm and it writes bubble sort most of the time. Activation steering is often used to push a model toward less obvious solutions. Does a steering direction that points away from the default spread the model over the algorithms it knows, or does it hand the default's share to one alternative?

It hands it to one alternative. The paper builds a and froze, before any steered program existed, the strengths, the decision rules and which family should gain. On a with fresh seeds, sorting entropy over algorithm families fell below the mean of five by

Lower than random pushes of the same size is the signature of selection, not flattening. Every passing program outside the labelled families that a blind judge checked was a textbook algorithm.

                        What the paper does not show

                        • The selection result is measured on one model, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, and two prompts, each with one wording. The steering test was not run on gemma-2-2b-it, where the negative-instruction results did not reproduce the Qwen pattern.
                        • The SELECT rule accepted the top prediction of either of two frozen rankings, which loosens it, and on path search the s2 operating point missed the frozen pass-rate bar (0.17 against 0.25).
                        • On path search the labeller agrees with a blind judge at kappa 0.39 on steered outputs, so the exact A* share is uncertain; the sorting result, at kappa 0.94, is the cleaner of the two.
                        • Novelty was measured as correct code outside known algorithm families, which is near zero by construction on textbook tasks. Only the two-family experiment had a judge check the passing programs in the labeller's residual class; 11 such programs from the later experiments were not judged. The result says these controls did not create new algorithms for path search and sorting, not that steering cannot raise novelty on open problems.
                        • The layer band was chosen by a probe whose accuracy was flat across layers, and the window covers the first 64 generated tokens; other bands or windows may flatten where this one selects.
                        • The point at which the model commits to an idea is not located: probes on the first eight generated tokens were at chance.
                        • Truncation affects labels: continuing 150 truncated programs flipped 10.7% of labels in the temperature experiments, and batch composition alone flips 11% to 17% of labels in repeated runs.

                        Where each view's data comes from

                        • The finding, the random-direction comparison, the stepper, the strength rule, the correctness and off-menu views: gen_art_experiment_6/results/selector_tables.json (per-condition counts, pass rates, entropies, bootstrap differences and CIs, frozen rankings, calibration runs, rule verdicts) and gen_art_experiment_6/results/frozen_selector_qwen_alphas.json (calibration mode shares and pass rates).
                        • The program browser and the stepper's example: gen_art_experiment_6/full_method_out.json, Qwen datasets, seeds 0 to 149 of the baseline and of the steered and random conditions. Responses are cut to their first 900 characters for size; labels and oracle results are from the file. Random draws 2 to 5 and the temperature cells carry labels only.
                        • Temperature: gen_art_experiment_4/results/temperature_law_redraw.json (cells and the ideas-against-phrasings table, fresh-seed redraw, n = 100 per cell).
                        • Negative instructions: gen_art_experiment_5/full_method_out.json (labels of the confirmation programs, counted per condition, three placebo blocks pooled) and gen_art_experiment_5/results/regularity.json (Fisher tests with Holm correction).
